title: Numerical Riemann--Hurwitz with a nonnegative different term
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X,Y$ be smooth proper geometrically integral curves of dimension one over $k$ [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a nonconstant $k$-morphism, meaning it does not factor through a $k$-rational point of $Y$, and suppose its induced extension of function fields $k(X)/k(Y)$ is finite separable [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower]. Put $d=[k(X):k(Y)]$, the dimension of $k(X)$ over $k(Y)$, and put $g(Z)=\dim_kH^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ for $Z=X,Y$ [def-sc-genus]. Then $d$ is a positive integer and there exists an integer $r\geq0$ such that
$$2g(X)-2=d\bigl(2g(Y)-2\bigr)+r.$$
No tameness assumption or hypothesis that $d$ is invertible in $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C1B (curves-section-riemann-hurewitz), displayed equality with r = degree of the effective different divisor; Tag 0C1C (curves-lemma-generically-etale), equivalence with finite separability. Proper curves are projective by varieties.tex Tag 0A26 (varieties-lemma-dim-1-proper-projective).

proof.text: The function-field extension in the hypotheses is induced by $f$, so $f$ is dominant. It is finite by hypothesis. Its dimension $d$ is a natural number and is positive: the singleton consisting of $1\in k(X)$ is linearly independent over $k(Y)$, since $a\cdot1=0$ implies $a=0$. Thus a basis has at least one element.

source.place: Tag 0C1B (curves-section-riemann-hurewitz), degree of the nonconstant map; elementary field linear algebra.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-differential-euler-degree] to $Z=X,Y$: integrality ensures nonempty connectedness, and smoothness, properness and dimension one are assumed. Thus the relative differential sheaves are invertible and $\deg_k\Omega_{Z/k}=2g(Z)-2$. Set $B=\Omega_{X/k}$ and $A=f^*\Omega_{Y/k}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1), $A$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0C1B (curves-section-riemann-hurewitz), numerical degree calculation, assembled from the separate line-bundle and degree-comparison arguments.

proof.text: The dominant map $f$ induces the finite separable function-field extension in the hypotheses. Therefore [lem-sfb-separable-curve-differential-nonzero] gives a nonzero map $\mathrm df:A\to B$.

Apply [lem-sfb-curve-nonzero-line-map-degree] to $\mathrm df$ on the proper integral dimension-one curve $X$. It supplies the invertible bundle $L=B\otimes A^\vee$ and its nonzero section. Put $r=\deg_k L\in\mathbf Z$. The same lemma gives $r\ge0$ and $r=\deg_k B-\deg_k A$.

By [lem-sfb-proper-curve-bundle-pullback-degree], applied to the invertible $\Omega_{Y/k}$, $\deg_k A=d\deg_k\Omega_{Y/k}$: $X,Y$ are proper integral curves, $f$ is dominant and the induced extension is finite. Substitution of Step 2 into Step 4 yields $r=(2g(X)-2)-d(2g(Y)-2)$, hence the asserted equality. Step 1 gives $d>0$ and Step 4 gives $r\ge0$. No tameness or invertibility of $d$ is used.
